chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I do not reach the Black Stone.' He said, 'When you perform the obligatory Tawaf, it will not harm you.'

key_terms.يَضُرُّكَ: It will harm you / be detrimental to you

ai.seo_question: Does missing the Black Stone invalidate the obligatory Hajj circumambulation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that if a worshipper is unable to reach the Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad) to touch or kiss it during the obligatory circumambulation (Tawaf al-Faridhah), their Tawaf remains valid and is not invalidated by this omission. This ruling highlights the distinction between the recommended acts (Sunnah) of touching the Stone and the core validity of the ritual, ensuring that physical crowding or mobility issues do not burden the believer. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (Yusr) in worship, where the intention and completion of the circuit suffice when the specific act is hindered by circumstances.
